predecessors.name: Kingdom of Powys
predecessors.text: the northern portion of Powys, Maelor and Yale first, later with Nanheudwy, Cynllaith, Glyndyfrdwy and Mochnant Is Rhaeadr (page); drawn as the Maelor and Yale cells

successors.name: Kingdom of England
successors.text: the marcher lordships formed from northern Powys (Bromfield and Yale among them)

ledger.x: 1160: Madog ap Maredudd dies and Powys splits; the northern half becomes Powys Fadog.
1169: Glyndyfrdwy joins the realm in Cliopatria's first Fadog shape.
1191: the northern realm becomes known as Powys Fadog under Madog ap Gruffudd.
1210: Cynllaith and Mochnant Is Rhaeadr are in the realm in Cliopatria's 1210 shape, which adds the Llansilin cell that its Powys Wenwynwyn shape held to 1209.
1258: Gruffydd II is forced into Llywelyn ap Gruffudd's alliance.
1277: Llywelyn ap Gruffudd loses northern Powys.
1277: Llywelyn Fychan and Gruffudd Fychan I accept English overlordship and divide the realm.
1284: the Statute of Rhuddlan ends the English-held princely lordships of northern Powys.
1284: the Statute of Rhuddlan abolishes the princely territories of Wales.
1284: the principality of Powys Fadog ends.

wars.name: Edward I's first Welsh war
wars.outcome: 'By 1276 northern Powys was in disorder, with brother fighting brother'; Madog II submitted, Henry de Lacy took Dinas Bran on 10 May 1277 and the castle was dismantled; Madog II died in battle later that year and the realm was divided between his brother…

wars.name: Edward I's conquest of Wales
wars.outcome: In 1282, 'during the final campaign of Llywelyn ap Gruffudd, all of the rulers of northern Powys would once again turn against England'; the Statute of Rhuddlan of 1284 abolished the remaining princely titles and territories.

certainty.note: The commote boundaries are approximate and no treaty line is on the pages; the lordship frontiers with Shropshire and Cheshire (the Dee, Offa's Dyke) are unsurveyed.
